Cross-validate a GWR with spatial folds

Source: R/cross-validation.R
cv_gwr.Rd

Refits a geographically weighted regression from scratch on each training fold and scores it on the held-out fold, so the reported error is the model's at locations it did not see. Use it for an accuracy figure for a GWR: the in-sample \(R^2\) that model_metrics() reports on a gwr_fit says little, because a local regression with a small bandwidth can track the training points almost exactly. The bandwidth is selected again in each fold unless bandwidth fixes it, so the selection itself is inside the cross-validation, with no tuning on the full data first.

Usage

cv_gwr(
  data_sf,
  response_var,
  predictor_vars,
  folds = NULL,
  k = 5,
  seed = 123,
  adaptive = TRUE,
  bandwidth = NULL,
  kernel = c("bisquare", "gaussian", "tricube", "boxcar", "exponential"),
  boundary = NULL,
  pointize = "auto",
  block_size = NULL,
  auto_range = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  metrics = NULL
)

Arguments

data_sf

An sf layer with the response and the predictors.

response_var

Name of the response column.

predictor_vars

Character vector of predictor column names.

folds

Optional fold definitions, in one of three shapes: a make_folds() result; a bare list of list(train =, test =) pairs of ..row_id values; or a vector of fold labels, one per row, which becomes leave-that-label-out splits. The label vector is how folds built by another package are used here: blockCV::cv_spatial() returns one as $folds_ids, while its $folds_list holds two unnamed vectors per fold and is refused by name. Train and test must be disjoint; a fold that trains on its own test rows is not a cross-validation split and is refused with an error. IDs naming no row of the prepared data are dropped with a logged count (expected when rows were removed for missing values; a sign the folds came from other data when they were not). When NULL, the folds are make_folds(method = "block_kfold"), built with k, seed, boundary, block_size and auto_range. With folds = NULL the score estimates the error at the distance the block grid built here puts between the held-out points and their training data, which overstates the error of a map where the samples cover the area it predicts over. The excess is how much the model's error grows from the map's distances to the data to the block grid's, and is small for a model whose error changes little with the distance from the data. fold_separation() with prediction_points compares the held-out distances with those of the locations the model will predict at, and make_folds(method = "knndm", prediction_points = ) builds folds matched to them.

k

Number of folds to build when folds is NULL; not read when folds is supplied. Default 5.

seed

Seed for building the folds when folds is NULL, and for the one seed drawn per fold before it is fitted. With a seed, the caller's random stream is restored afterwards. Default 123.

adaptive

Logical; use an adaptive bandwidth, a number of neighbours, rather than a fixed distance. Default TRUE.

bandwidth

Optional bandwidth, applied to every fold. For adaptive = TRUE a whole number of neighbours; for adaptive = FALSE a distance in the units of the projected CRS the folds are fitted in (lon/lat input is projected first, so a value in degrees is read as metres). NULL (default) selects a bandwidth in each fold from that fold's training rows, by the search fit_gwr_model() runs (its section "Bandwidth selection": AICc, or the leave-one-location-out sum of squares when observations share a location), and reports it in fold_metrics$bandwidth.

kernel

The kernel that weights each location's neighbours: "bisquare" (default), "gaussian", "tricube", "boxcar" or "exponential", as in fit_gwr_model().

boundary

Optional polygon layer (sf or sfc). Data without a CRS are aligned to it, and the blocks built when folds is NULL are clipped to it (see make_folds() and spatialkit-geometry).

pointize

How a feature that is not a point is reduced to one before fitting: a mode of coerce_to_points(). Default "auto".

block_size

Optional minimum block edge length, in the units of the CRS the folds are built in, for the blocks built when folds is NULL; see make_folds(). It is a size you choose and is compared with the autocorrelation range only when one can be estimated, in which case a smaller size is warned about. Beside supplied folds it has nothing to size and raises a warning of class spatialkit_fold_args_ignored.

auto_range

Logical, default FALSE. TRUE with folds = NULL estimates the autocorrelation range and uses it as the minimum block size. TRUE beside supplied folds raises the same warning as block_size.

parallel

Accepted so that every cv_*() function takes the same arguments, but the GWR folds always run one after another in this R process, where the warnings predict() raises for each fold are collected into one. A value asking for more than one core raises a warning saying so. Default FALSE.

metrics

Optional scoring function of your own, a function(y, yhat) returning a named numeric vector; its names become columns of fold_metrics (per fold) and overall (pooled) beside the built-in ones. See the section "Your own metrics" in cv_spatial() for the contract.

Value

A list with the elements cv_spatial() returns (overall, fold_metrics, predictions, folds, n_folds_attempted, n_folds_succeeded, fold_status, orphan_rows, n_unknown_ids and n_dropped; see its Value for each, and for the five fold statuses), plus:

formula

The model formula, as text.

adaptive

Whether the bandwidth was adaptive.

fold_metrics also carries each fold's bandwidth. Adj_R2 is NA in both overall and fold_metrics: the pooled predictions have no single parameter count, and a GWR's effective parameter count is not its predictor count.

A held-out location whose local regression cannot be estimated has yhat NA, and one beyond the reach of its fold's fit is predicted and scored; each case raises one warning for the whole run (classes "spatialkit_gwr_not_estimable" and "spatialkit_gwr_extrapolation"), with the totals over the folds that had any. See predict.gwr_fit(). Where a fold's fit took the response about a centre (a response at a large offset; see fit_gwr_model()), predictions also carries y_centre (that centre, 0 in the rows of a fold fitted on the raw response), yhat_centred and y_train_mean_centred (yhat and y_train_mean less the centre, which keep digits that rounding at the response's size would lose), and the metrics are those of the centred values, as model_metrics() computes them.

Details

Folds default to spatial blocks (make_folds(method = "block_kfold")), not random ones. A random split leaves a held-out point's neighbours in the training set, so its score is the error of predicting among the samples; blocks hold out whole areas, and folds says what their score estimates. Use cv_bayes() for the same treatment of a Bayesian GP, cv_rf() for a random forest, and compare_models_cv() to score several backends on one set of folds.

Percentage errors on responses with zeros

MAPE divides by the observed value and SMAPE by \(|y| + |\hat{y}|\), so neither is defined where its denominator is zero. Neither returns Inf or NaN. Both are averaged over the rows whose denominator is non-zero, and are NA when no row qualifies. Non-zero is judged at the scale of the data: a denominator no larger than 100 machine epsilons times the largest one counts as zero, so the rule does not depend on the units of the response. The n_MAPE and n_SMAPE columns record how many rows that was; the n column (n_pred in a cross-validation result) counts finite observation/prediction pairs. Read a percentage error next to that count: when n_MAPE is smaller, MAPE is an average over a subset of the data, whatever its value.

Any response taking exact zeros is affected: counts, rainfall, abundance, claim amounts. On a zero-inflated response with 62 zeros out of 120, MAPE averages the 58 non-zero rows and n_MAPE is 58. SMAPE drops the rows where observation and prediction are both near zero, which on a well-fitted zero-inflated model are the rows it got right, so it averages the harder rows only and reads worse than the fit deserves. n_SMAPE shows how many rows it kept; it does not correct the average.

RMSE, MAE and \(R^2\) use every finite row; prefer them whenever the response can be zero. For a Bayesian GP fit, cv_bayes() also reports CRPS and interval coverage, which are proper scoring rules and are defined at zero.

See also

Other cross-validation: compare_models_cv(), cv_bayes(), cv_rf(), cv_spatial(), plot_calibration(), plot_cv_metrics()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
n <- 60
dat <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),
             elev = rnorm(n)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
dat$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) +
  2 * dat$elev + rnorm(n)
cv <- cv_gwr(dat, "price", "elev", k = 3, bandwidth = 30)
#> cv_gwr(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3).
cv$overall          # pooled over the held-out rows of every fold
#>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE       R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE
#> 1 1.970881 1.640318 11.65992 11.14015 0.620296     NA     60     60      60
cv$fold_metrics     # and fold by fold
#>   fold n_train n_test n_pred    RMSE      MAE      MAPE     SMAPE        R2
#> 1    1      39     21     21 1.34471 1.167010  7.532286  7.606738 0.6918865
#> 2    2      41     19     19 2.31357 1.985458 14.905985 13.676105 0.5117606
#> 3    3      40     20     20 2.16090 1.809408 12.910182 12.441061 0.6691330
#>   Adj_R2 n_MAPE n_SMAPE bandwidth
#> 1     NA     21      21        30
#> 2     NA     19      19        30
#> 3     NA     20      20        30
